The narrator, an original elderly storyteller of about seventy with Middle Eastern features, weathered warm olive skin with deep lines on the forehead, kind deep-set brown eyes, a very long silver-white beard and long silver hair under a hooded brown wool robe, seated cross-legged by a small campfire at night under a starry desert sky, holding an old rolled scroll in both hands, holds his head level and looks straight into the camera, his lips closed, silent, a faint warm smile, breathing slowly. thresholds.rule: MOUTH_TALKING when spread > 0.016 AND motion > 0.0032; FACE_NOT_FOUND when the face is in < 80 % of the frames (unchanged from the lips check)
thresholds.why: spread: closed 0.0025-0.0045 vs talking >= 0.056 (geometric middle 0.016); motion: closed <= 0.0025 vs talking >= 0.0041 (the Keeper's >= 0.0087; middle 0.0032). The spread alone would flag a mouth that settles once from the open talking reference (0.041-0.066, motion 0.0006-0.0025): talking is wide and fast

findings: with the approved mouth-closed front reference the face landmarker found his face in 2-27 % of the frames: 4 of 4 FACE_NOT_FOUND, whatever the gaze or the light (dark hood, side firelight, the beard over a closed mouth); a voice-over shot built that way would fail the run

with the talking reference (storyteller-ref.jpg, his `talk_refs` frame) facing the lens: face 100 %, the mouth starts as in the reference (opening 0.061) and settles closed within 2.5 s, then stays closed (0.002) to the end: passes (spread 0.041, motion 0.0006)
with the talking reference looking down into the fire: face 17 %, FACE_NOT_FOUND

so a voice-over Keeper uses his talking frame and faces the lens on a static camera (plan_check KEEPER_VO_POSE); the owner's 'into the fire' and 'closing the scroll' become the fire beside him and the scroll rolled closed while he faces the camera
